views.rationale: AAPL's year-over-year growth in selling, general and administrative expense was driven primarily by an increase in headcount-related expenses and higher spending on marketing and advertising and infrastructure-related costs, whereas AMZN's sales growth was driven by increased customer usage, partially offset by pricing changes.

BAC's revenue declined $106 million to $4.1 billion due to lower sales and trading revenue and lower investment banking fees, whereas CAT's second-quarter 2019 sales and revenues were $14.432 billion, a 3 percent increase from second-quarter 2018 sales and revenues of $14.011 billion.
